sites.fact: the CloseFrame constructor runs setReason("") + setCode(NORMAL), so the frame's payload buffer is [0x03,0xE8]

setPayload OVERRIDES the base method and assigns only the code/reason FIELDS - it never calls super.setPayload, so a DECODED close frame object keeps the constructor payload. This is the mechanism behind quirk Q10.
a 1-byte close payload sets code = PROTOCOL_ERROR (1002)
isValid() does NOT reject 1002, so a 1-byte close raises no exception at translate time
updatePayload composes the payload as the low two bytes of the code (big-endian) followed by the UTF-8 reason
processFrameClosing reads cf.getCloseCode()/cf.getMessage() (1055-1060) and, when the state is not CLOSING, calls webSocketImpl.close(code, reason, true) for a TWOWAY draft (1067-1068)
close(int,String,boolean) is the single method both a LOCAL close and the inbound-close echo go through

it builds a BRAND NEW frame: new CloseFrame(); setReason(message); setCode(code); isValid(); sendFrame(closeFrame) - so the wire payload is the RECEIVED code and reason, never the received frame object

java_sites_verified.prompt_hypothesis_corrected: The task prompt guessed the full stack reaches its own close frame 'after the close-payload parse throws InvalidDataException'. That is NOT what the pinned source does and the guess was not adopted: CloseFrame.setPayload maps a 1-byte payload to 1002 (CloseFrame.java:252-253) and isValid accepts 1002 (CloseFrame.java:226-243), so NOTHING throws. The full stack reaches WebSocketImpl.close by the ORDINARY processFrameClosing path with code=1002, and that method composes its own frame. The fix implements the verified path, not the guess.
java_sites_verified.why_ws_core_legitimately_differs: The core's Q19/Q10 echo is pinned to the java-oracle harness, which re-emits the RECEIVED CloseFrame object (java-oracle/src/main/java/OracleEngine.java:382, emitOutbound(List.of(frame), index, "echo_close")). Because CloseFrame.setPayload never writes super's buffer, that object's payload really is [0x03,0xE8] - so the core observable is CORRECT AT ITS LAYER and its 74/74 live-oracle confirmation stands. The harness's echo COMPOSITION, however, is the harness's, not WebSocketImpl's. Full-stack composition therefore belongs one layer up, exactly like the US-015 automatic pong.

Review round 2 caught a WRONG Java mechanism in the sequence-34 ledger preimage: it claimed Java decodes and dispatches one frame at a time. The pinned source shows a two-phase decode — translateFrame returns every complete frame in the chop, then decodeFrames dispatches them — so the poisoned frame is decoded BEFORE the echo is enqueued and only dispatched after it. The preimage was corrected and rehashed. The finding was verified against the source rather than adopted on the reviewer's word, and the corrected record states the mechanism more precisely than either version.

review_round_2.verdict_received: BLOCK — exactly one blocking finding; the close-composition implementation and all six other verification areas PASSED
review_round_2.finding_verbatim: Sequence 34 hashes an incorrect Java mechanism: internal/deltaledger/definitions_autobahn.go:97 says Java decodes one frame at a time and flushes the echo before decoding the poisoned frame, but Draft_6455.translateFrame translates all complete frames first and WebSocketImpl.decodeFrames only then dispatches them sequentially. The accurate mechanism is echo enqueue during earlier processFrame dispatch, followed by the later sequence failure and flushAndClose draining queued output. Correct the preimage and regenerate sequence 34, the ledger head, plan binding, and dependent fixtures.

my_independent_source_reading.method: Read Draft_6455.translateFrame, WebSocketImpl.decodeFrames, Draft_6455.processFrame/processFrameContinuousAndNonFin, WebSocketImpl.send/write/outQueue, close(InvalidDataException) and flushAndClose directly in the digest-pinned quarantined 1.6.0 tree, rather than adopting either the original preimage or the reviewer's wording on trust.
my_independent_source_reading.agreement: The reviewer is RIGHT on the load-bearing point and my original preimage was WRONG. Java decodes in two phases: WebSocketImpl.decodeFrames calls draft.translateFrame ONCE (WebSocketImpl.java:394), and Draft_6455.translateFrame (drafts/Draft_6455.java:724-773) loops translateSingleFrame over the whole buffer and returns a List of EVERY complete frame in the chop; only then does decodeFrames dispatch them with for (Framedata f : frames) draft.processFrame(this, f) (WebSocketImpl.java:395-398). So the poisoned frame is DECODED before the echo exists — it is merely DISPATCHED later. My original 'decodes and dispatches ONE frame at a time' was false.
refinements_i_add_beyond_the_reviewers_w: WHY the poison survives phase 1 (the reviewer did not say): the 5.15 poison is a SEQUENCE error, not a decode error. A lone CONTINUATION frame is structurally valid to translateSingleFrame, so it translates cleanly and only fails in phase 2.

The exact throw site: Draft_6455.processFrameContinuousAndNonFin's currentContinuousFrame == null arm at drafts/Draft_6455.java:934-937. This is the FIN=false arm, and Autobahn 5.15's own case description in the per-case report says 'Continuation Frame with FIN = false where there is nothing to continue' — so it is NOT the processFrameIsFin twin at :1001-1004. My round-1 rationale had also loosely called it 'a dangling continuation' without pinning FIN.

Enqueue path made explicit: dispatching the SECOND fragment completes the message (processFrameIsFin -> onWebsocketMessage), the echo listener's send runs WebSocketImpl.send(Collection):667-681 -> write(List):749-755 -> write(ByteBuffer):736-742, doing outQueue.add at :740 and wsl.onWriteDemand at :741 — all before the third frame is dispatched.

Failure path made explicit: processFrame throws, decodeFrames catches at WebSocketImpl.java:405-408 and calls close(e) -> close(1002,...) (:631-633 -> :463), which enqueues Java's OWN close frame (:482-486) and then calls flushAndClose (:494).

One precision where I state it slightly differently from the reviewer: flushAndClose does not itself drain the queue — it raises the final write demand, wsl.onWriteDemand(this) at WebSocketImpl.java:594-595, whose in-source comment reads 'ensures that all outgoing frames are flushed before closing the connection'; the actual socket drain is performed by the listener's write path servicing that demand. The reviewer's 'flushAndClose draining queued output' is right in effect; the record now states the mechanism precisely. This is a refinement, not a disagreement.

The Rust side is sharper than the round-1 preimage claimed. It does NOT 'suppress queued output': the echo is never ENQUEUED at all, because ws_core's typed failure short-circuits the poll before the completed message's Text event is delivered (ws_driver finish_poll returns DriverOutput::Failure without draining queued events, rust/ws-driver/src/lib.rs:599-611; rust/ws-testee/src/io_loop.rs:221-225 then shuts the socket and breaks), so the adapter's event-driven echo policy never runs. Confirmed empirically, not just by reading: the 5.15 adapter session line reads texts=0 (evidence/rust/autobahn-e5b/serve-run2.log session=7).

The Java observable is better founded than 7.3.2's. The 5.15 per-case report's own expectation map is {NON-STRICT: [], OK: [['message','fragment1fragment2',false]]}, so the Java receipt's OK class ENTAILS that live Java echoed the completed message — a single admissible observable, unlike 7.3.2 where OK admitted 1002-or-drop. The record now says so.
